display: Kmodern gateway build pass (emits CommonJS into dist/)
//: The build-only compiler pass, kept apart from tsconfig.json so the one that serves `typecheck`
does not also have to serve the build: the two change for different reasons, and a build that
has to accommodate the typecheck project's test files ships them.
module: commonjs is not a style choice, it is forced twice over.
1. NestJS dependency injection reads `design:paramtypes`, which only a real TypeScript emit
produces. esbuild cannot emit it, so running this app through tsx builds the object graph
successfully and then injects `undefined` into every constructor — a silent failure that
looks like a working boot. Verified, not assumed.
2. The generated Prisma client is TypeScript source whose relative imports carry no file
extension, so `module: nodenext` rejects it outright. CommonJS resolves extensionless
specifiers natively, which is the only reason this configuration is possible at all.
The Prisma generator is therefore pinned to `moduleFormat = "cjs"` in prisma/schema.prisma.
Without it the generated client uses `import.meta.url` to locate its query engine, and that
is a hard SyntaxError in CommonJS — so the two settings have to move together.
`paths` exists only so the typechecker can see through packages/schema's exports map, which
node10 resolution does not understand. It bridges types; it has no runtime effect.
rootDir is the repository root, not src/, because the workspace packages this app imports
are source-only TypeScript and enter the program. They are emitted alongside the app, which
is what makes dist/ runnable without a bundler: those packages have no compiled form of their
own until the kernel phase converts them, and a Node process cannot require() TypeScript.
The emitted entry point is dist/apps/api/src/main.js, and dist/ needs a package.json marking
it CommonJS because this package declares "type": "module". The build writes both.
